summary.headline: Vinati Organics FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 17% to INR741 crores and PAT 18% to INR488 crores, with the company still debt-free.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone net income including other income rose 17% QoQ to INR631 crores, EBITDA grew 20% QoQ to INR203 crores and PAT rose 27% QoQ to INR137 crores. For FY26, standalone net income was flat at INR2,281 crores while EBITDA and PAT grew 17% and 18%. Demand softened from October 2025 and management says it has since recovered. IBB volumes fell about 20% versus FY25 because of raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, which management says is now resolved. Management guides about 15% company-level volume growth in FY27 and FY27 capex of INR200-250 crores.

segments.name: ATBS
segments.commentary: Roughly one-third of FY26 revenue; management expects about 15% volume growth YoY for at least the next three years. Plant running at about 80% utilisation (about 75% post-expansion). Phase 2 of the expansion comes into effect by October 2026, with fuller utilisation in FY28.

segments.name: Antioxidants (AO)
segments.commentary: Roughly 15-20% of FY26 revenue; revenue grew 15% in FY26. Management said FY26 AO volume was roughly flat-to-5% up, and the anti-dumping duty (ADD) application was rejected and reapplied, with a decision 6-9 months away.

segments.name: IB and HP-MTBE
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; stable in FY26, with management expecting double-digit growth in FY27.

segments.name: IBB
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; volume fell about 20% versus FY25 due to raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, now reported as resolved.

segments.name: Butyl phenols
segments.commentary: Capacity about 50,000 tonnes running at roughly 70-75% utilisation; management expects moderate growth in FY27 with no room for further expansion, so incremental demand goes first to captive use.

segments.name: Customised and others
segments.commentary: Grew 10% YoY in FY26 on higher customer demand. Remainder of revenue mix.

segments.name: VOPL (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales were only about INR10 crores. Process reengineering of about 6 months to finish by September 2026, with production from October and revenue of about INR100-120 crores expected in FY27, from Q2/Q3.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company-level volume growth guided at about 15%.
ATBS volume growth of about 15% YoY expected for at least the next three years.
FY27 capex earmarked at INR200-250 crores (about INR200 crores at Vinati Organics and INR40-50 crores at VOPL); management says about INR250-300 crores a year for 3-5 years.
AO and butyl phenol revenue targeted at INR800-900 crores in the next two years.
Long-term EBITDA margin of 26-27% considered achievable, given expansions, new products and raw material swings.
Gross block addition of about INR500 crores assumed at 1:1 asset turn.
Two to three new downstream products expected in H2 FY27, with revenue mainly from FY28.
Company will continue to fund expansion from internal accruals and remain debt-free.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR270 crores, including VOPL capacity expansion, new product development and operational scalability. The ATBS capacity expansion was completed during FY26.

ATBS: a Phase 1 of 10,000 tonnes is commissioned. Total ATBS capacity is about 50,000 tonnes for lower molecular weight grades and about 40,000 tonnes for higher purity grades. Phase 2 (another 10,000 tonnes) expected by October 2026. Two-phase cost about INR250-300 crores.
CWIP was about INR210 crores at year-end, of which about INR60-70 crores is yet to be capitalised at VOPL. About INR120-125 crores of VOPL CWIP is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

Pipeline products are downstream derivatives of MEHQ, butyl phenols and antioxidants, plus TAA, PTAP and 4-MAP at VOPL. Isoamylene derivatives were dropped. Monomers and polymers are under consideration but not confirmed.
Butyl phenol capacity of about 50,000 tonnes is at 70-75% utilisation with no space to expand.
demand_pricing: Demand softened from October 2025. Management says demand has since recovered, and ATBS is still growing at double-digit rates industry-wide.
ATBS pricing is stable and follows a formula-based mechanism. Management says it passes raw material and logistics price moves through to customers and holds margins.

AO faces undercutting and aggressive selling by Chinese producers. Management says ADD was not granted and has been reapplied, and it notes that 80-90% of ADD applications were rejected in the sector.
Raw material and logistics availability normalised after early disruption from the Iran war in Feb 2026. Logistics is described as stable.
ATBS end-use spans polymers for enhanced oil recovery, superabsorbents, personal care, detergents, mining and water treatment. Vinati sells to polymer makers, not directly to oilfield operators.

qa_highlights.question: What new products are in the pipeline, and when will they come online?
qa_highlights.answer: Most are downstream niche chemicals for fragrance, personal care, food-additive and plastics users. Two or three products are due in H2 FY27, with revenue mainly from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 revenue mix by product?
qa_highlights.answer: ATBS is about one-third and AO is 15-20%. IB is 10-12%, IBB is 10-12%, and customised and other products make up the rest, with overall ATBS and AO together around 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VOPL revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VOPL sales were about INR10 crores in FY26. Management expects about INR100-120 crores in FY27 once reengineering finishes, with revenue from Q2/Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is planned in VOPL and how much CWIP is there?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR40-50 crores of the FY27 capex goes to VOPL and about INR200 crores to the parent. VOPL CWIP of about INR120-125 crores is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ATBS capacity and cost of the two expansion phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is about 50,000 tonnes (about 40,000 tonnes for higher-purity grades) with 10,000 tonnes per phase. The two phases cost about INR250-300 crores in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will AO and butyl phenol revenue reach the targeted INR700-800 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is on track, with AO and butyl phenol revenue in the INR800-900 crore range within the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 26-27% EBITDA margin is a reasonable long-term level given expansions, new products and raw material swings.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AO growth lagged, and what is the status of the ADD?
qa_highlights.answer: AO growth was about 5% in FY26 because of aggressive Chinese undercutting. ADD was not granted, has been reapplied, and a decision could take 6-9 months.

risks_watch: AO margins and volumes depend on the anti-dumping duty decision, which could take another 6-9 months after reapplication, while Chinese players undercut prices.
VOPL revenue of INR100-120 crores in FY27 depends on finishing process reengineering by September 2026. The plant had teething troubles with its new process.
ATBS Phase 2 utilisation is expected to build mainly in FY28, and the plant is running at about 75-80% utilisation.
Butyl phenol capacity is at 70-75% utilisation with no room to expand, so growth may cut merchant sales.
Sector cyclicality has shortened, with sharp swings in raw material prices, logistics and customer destocking.
Management guidance rests on about 15% volume growth, a recovery from the October 2025 slowdown and IBB volumes resuming after the Iran war disruption.

key_quotes: I think I've maintained an EBITDA margin of 26% to 27% because given expansions, new products, raw material fluctuations, I think that's a reasonably achievable EBITDA margin on a long-term basis.
So first of all, we did not hear back for the ADD on antioxidants, which means it was rejected. We have reapplied again for it because we have a strong case.
Basically, we went for a new process. And we faced some teething troubles there, and then we went to the main consultant and realizing some reengineering is required.
We are looking at organic expansion. We have a good pipeline of products, products under commissioning as well as products in the R&D phase.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the balance sheet, ATBS demand, margins and the debt-free funding model, and openly acknowledges the slowdown from October 2025. Cautious and somewhat evasive on AO growth and the anti-dumping duty outcome, and on the VOPL timeline, which management said had hit teething troubles and was being re-engineered.
